_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. The credential store, config and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own secret-echo funnel, which is removed. Classes closed, each by a built-binary test seen failing on the pre-kit build: an API error that echoes the key, a piece of it, base64 or URL-encoded (TestAPIErrorEchoOfKeyIsWithheld, CLI, --agent and MCP); a run-profile value under a declared credential name held at startup (TestProfileCredentialValueHeldAtStartup); a held credential refused to another origin and over plain http (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP); SPACEFAST_TOKEN held (TestSpacefastTokenHeld); the learn journal and the feedback ledger never record a held credential (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential, TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded). A malformed config's key stays held at startup (TestMalformedConfigCredentialHeldAtStartup, a guard: the pre-kit build already passed it). In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the seams swap (credkit_seam_test.go in cli, mcp, client). The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to the _length_limit DSN parameter, and the store runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: doctor reports a 403 from the credential probe as `WARN scope-limited`, so --fail-on warn sees it.
handfixes.why: doctorExitForFailOn reads the verdict's prefix. The generated line starts with `scope-limited`, which carries no prefix, so a key that cannot read the probe endpoint passed --fail-on warn and looked healthy to a script. TestDoctorScopeLimitedCredentialIsAWarning pins it. A reprint regenerates doctor_verdict.go and the fleet replay can re-create the unprefixed line.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the doctor verdict template should prefix the scope-limited line with WARN.
